title: The Agreement Layer for the Modern Agentic Enterprise
summary: Docusign will make its Iris-backed MCP Server generally available September 30 to Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot, Slack, and other MCP clients.

title: Orchestrating the Agentic SOC: A Practical Guide to Model Context Protocol
summary: Cortex can import and hourly-sync external MCP tools, with permission controls and human approval enabled by default for sensitive actions.

title: Amazon Quick adds new tool settings and Model Context Protocol (MCP) sync support for connectors
summary: Amazon Quick added per-tool enablement, consent settings, and synchronization as connected MCP servers change.

title: Anthropic makes first move into physical AI with new way for scientists, manufacturers to bring equipment to life
summary: Fortune reports that Anthropic’s model-agnostic Model Hardware Standard research preview builds on MCP to connect AI models with laboratory and manufacturing equipment.

title: The New MCP Roadmap
summary: Maintainers prioritize agentic messaging, HTTP-native transport, agent identity, improved primitives, and SDK usability.

title: The next generation of MCP
summary: Cloudflare explains how the stateless specification simplifies Workers deployment and replaces McpAgent with createMcpHandler where application state is unnecessary.

title: Scaling AI Agent Infrastructure with the MCP Stateless updates
summary: Google describes how removing protocol sessions enables ordinary load balancing, serverless deployment, failover, and header-based routing.

summary: Willison assesses stateless MCP and introduces mcp-explorer, datasette-mcp, and llm-mcp-client.

title: The 2026-07-28 Specification
summary: The release introduced a stateless core, MRTR, HTTP routing headers, cacheable lists, authorization hardening, extensions, and updated Tier 1 SDKs.

title: Beta SDKs for the 2026-07-28 MCP Spec Release Candidate Are Here
summary: Python, TypeScript, Go, and C# beta SDKs implemented the forthcoming stateless revision with opt-in migration paths.

title: The New MCP Specification: What Security Teams Must Prepare For
summary: Akamai finds that the revision removes session hijacking and unsolicited prompts but creates implementation risks around workflow state, headers, apps, and asynchronous tasks.
